title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-03-28
content:
Week: 2026-03-22 — 2026-03-28
Owner: Asha Patel (SRE)
Summary: Week focused on two main things: (1) triage and postmortem work for the P99 latency spike on hosted-api, (2) prep for kernel/driver maintenance on dedicated gpu pools. Routine on-call handoffs and SLO checks, small follow-ups from last week's canary.

Incidents
1) P99 latency spike — hosted-api (2026-03-23) — Sev2
- Timeline: 03/23 10:13 UTC first alerts; peak impact 10:20–10:55 UTC; mitigation fully in place by 11:05 UTC.
- Impact: elevated P95/P99 for text-generation routes (mainly gpt-like 2k seq workloads). Errors stayed low; no client-facing 5xx surge. Roughly 18% of requests experienced >250ms added latency at P99.
- Root cause (short): autoscaler change + kernel driver quirk led to imbalanced batching and delayed worker wakeups on a subset of nodes. The autoscaler change attempted to be more aggressive about bin-packing; combined with an edge-case in kernel GPU driver scheduling triggered longer preemption windows.
- Tickets / artifacts: SRE-3490 (incident), PR infra#468 (revert autoscaler packing change), confluence incident doc.
- Mitigation: roll back autoscaler packing change (hotfix PR merged), increase watchdog frequency for worker health checks, temporary adjustment of batching thresholds to favor lower latency for interactive routes.
- Follow-ups / action items:
  * Action SRE-3498: Add unit/integration tests for packing heuristic (owner: Miguel, eta: 2026-04-08).
  * Action SRE-3501: Add GPU driver scheduler detection and telemetry to identify nodes hitting preemption windows (owner: Liang, eta: 2026-04-02).
  * Action SRE-3502: Evaluate canary for packing heuristic with longer observation window (owner: Samira, eta: 2026-04-06).

2) Small DB maintenance outage during vacuum — dedicated control-plane (2026-03-25) — Sev3
- Short maintenance window mis-scheduled against a backup job; caused transient control-plane API 503s for ~7 minutes for a small percentage of Dedicated customers in eu-west-1.
- Root cause: missing guardrail in maintenance scheduler (ticket SRE-3510).
- Mitigation: added scheduler guardrail and improved runbook.
- Follow-up: SRE-3510 (owner: Samira, eta: 2026-04-01).

SLOs and Metrics
- Availability SLO (control plane): target 99.95% monthly. March month-to-date: 99.97% (within target).
- Latency SLO (hosted text-generation P99 < 200ms): rolling 7-day P99 currently at ~210ms after spike — hit error budget on latency by small margin; still within availability budget.
- Error budget remaining (hosted-api latency budget for March): ~85% remaining after accounting for spike. Note: we'll re-evaluate if follow-up changes don't reduce P99.
- Throughput: token/sec cluster aggregate: 1.9M tokens/s peak (03/26), steady 1.2–1.4M tokens/s typical.

On-call handoffs / rotations
- This week on-call: week shift 03/22–03/28 primary: Miguel Herrera, secondary: Liang Zhou.
- Handoff notes: see quick bullet points — Miguel covered the P99 spikes and ran the rollback steps; Liang picked up driver telemetry work and started root cause dives. No open pages left overnight beyond monitoring tasks.
- Pager fatigue: increased paging for the latency class alerts after the change; will tune thresholds so we don't page for small transient blips during canaries (Action SRE-3503).

Operational / Deployments
- Reverted autoscaler packing change (infra#468) and deployed hotfix 03/23 11:05 UTC. Canary monitored 24h, then promoted to prod with adjusted health gates.
- Upcoming kernel/driver maintenance for dedicated nodes in us-west-2 planned for 2026-04-03 02:00–05:00 UTC. Aim: apply vendor driver updates that should reduce preemption windows. Customers notified — see internal notice in #dedicated-ops.
- Canary plan: multi-stage canary for driver + autoscaler heuristic. Canary steps documented in confluence page linked above. Key extra step: extend canary observation to 4 hours for latency-sensitive routes.

Runbook / Alerts changes
- Added temporary alert suppression in canary clusters for low-severity autoscaler oscillations to avoid noisy pages. (Action SRE-3504)
- Introduced new metric slo_hosted_p99_increase_pct to better track relative regressions vs baseline.

Meeting notes / syncs
- SRE weekly sync (03/24): reviewed incident timeline, agreed on rollbacks and follow-ups. Decided to tighten canary window for packing changes.
- Postmortem review scheduled 2026-04-01 16:00 UTC — invite sent to infra, applied-ml, and product-hosted-api.
- On-call retrospective: need clearer escalation path to kernel/vendor team when driver-level anomalies are suspected. Action SRE-3511 assigned.

Items for next week
- Complete SRE-3490 postmortem and publish to Confluence (owner: Asha, due: 2026-04-01).
- Implement telemetry for GPU scheduler preemption windows (Liang, 2026-04-02).
- Finish tests for packing heuristic and run longer canary (Miguel, 2026-04-08).
- Prep for dedicated maintenance (Samira): customer comms, runbook update, rollback playbook.

Notes / informal
- A few TODOs in the runbook still use older CLI flags — will clean up before maintenance.
- Observed some noisy logs from worker-scheduler that are non-actionable; plan to filter at source rather than suppress alerts.
- Quick wins: short-term batching thresholds changed helped P99 get back closer to baseline; but still need kernel-level fix to fully eliminate tail.

Attachments & references
- Confluence incident doc (linked above).
- Jira: SRE-3490, SRE-3510, SRE-3501.
- PRs: infra#468 (revert), infra#472 (packaging tests).

If anything missing, ping #sre and I'll add notes.
